_comment: TEMPLATE. Copy to config.json in this skill's install context (`fleet where agent-revive` prints the directory) and replace every placeholder.
Everything install- and fleet-specific for tmux_triage.sh. The script takes the
AGENT NAME as an argument and resolves that agent's tmux session and service
unit from the templates below (with <agent> substituted). Point
AGENT_REVIVE_CONFIG at a copy of this file to drive a differently-laid-out fleet.
The only browser config here is WHERE stored profiles live
(accounts.profiles_dir). signin_driver/ reads the chosen account's password out
of accounts.pool_file below - the same pool the picker reads - and everything
else about the browser (headful, stealth, a virtual display, a throwaway profile
under the system temp dir when no stored one is asked for) is fixed by what
Google accepts and is therefore mechanism, not configuration. See SKILL.md step 6.
The PROMPT WORDING is NOT in here either. The auth-method menu, the 'Claude
account with subscription' option, the theme and scroll prompts and the
never-API rule are Claude Code's own UI, the same for every install, so they
live in SKILL.md as mechanism.
This skill owns NO credential. accounts.pool_file is the PATH to where the
fleet's Claude account pool already lives; the credentials stay outside this
tree. See secrets/claude-account-pool.example.json for the shape.
JSON has no comments, so every _comment key is documentation the loader strips.
Paths starting with ~/ expand against the account that runs the scripts; paths
containing <agent> have that token replaced with the agent name at run time.
How this fleet names each agent's tmux session and service unit, and where an
agent's own files live. These are fleet CONVENTIONS (still correct after a fresh
clone on the same fleet), so they are choices and belong here. The LIST of which
agents exist is machine state and is discovered ('ls' the agents home, 'tmux
ls'), never written down.
The session to drive, per agent. tmpdir MUST match the TMUX_TMPDIR the session
was created with, or tmux reports 'no server running' and every capture fails;
with TMUX_TMPDIR set, the socket resolves at <tmpdir>/tmux-<uid>/default. The
script drops $TMUX from the child env, because $TMUX (inherited when run from
inside a session) otherwise wins over TMUX_TMPDIR and reads the wrong server.
tmpdir is the FALLBACK: when the agent's unit can be read, its own
Environment=TMUX_TMPDIR (with %t expanded for its service manager) is used
instead (tmux_triage.sh --facts). <uid> is replaced with the numeric id of the
user running the scripts. The value below is the fleet unit template's user
form, /run/user/<uid>/claude-tmux-<agent>; an install that runs its agents as
SYSTEM units writes /run/claude-tmux-<agent>. On macOS (launchd has no runtime
directory) it is <agents-root>/run/claude-tmux-<agent>, written out in full, and
systemd_unit below holds the session job's launchd label,
<launchd_prefix>.session.<agent> (com.agent-fleet.session.<agent> by default).
The daemons a fleet agent keeps running so that something can WAKE it: an
inbound-message watcher, a scheduler. tmux_triage.sh reports, per entry,
whether a process whose command line carries `pattern` (a literal substring
of one argument, e.g. the script's path below its skills dir) runs with THIS
agent's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR in its environment - the dir resolved from the
service unit, else <agents_home>/<agent>/.claude. A ready prompt with EVERY
entry absent classifies `stopped` instead of `healthy`: the session is idle
and polling nothing, which the pane alone cannot tell from a quiet hour.
List every daemon ANY agent on the fleet runs. `stopped` needs ALL of them
absent, so an agent that runs only some of them reads healthy while those
run. An empty or absent list switches off only this per-entry reading:
`stopped` and `follower-down` still come from the per-follower reading
(SKILL.md), from the jobs `agent-daemons.py status <agent>` reports.
The two entries below are the scheduler and the Slack watcher, which is what
a fleet with Slack as its one working transport runs. The script column of
`python3 <fleet>/systemd/agent-daemons.py jobs` names every daemon's script;
its pattern is that script's path from the skills directory. Each further
working transport adds its watcher's line.
name: the key in the output's `daemons` object. An entry holding only
`_comment`, like this one, is documentation and is skipped; any other entry
without a non-empty name and pattern is a config error (exit 2), because a
daemon silently not checked is a false `healthy`.
The FOLLOWERS a session arms (`agent-daemons.py follow <agent> <job>`) need no
entry here: the triage derives the jobs the agent must follow from
`agent-daemons.py status <agent> --json` and reports each one (`followers`,
state `follower-down`), and the jobs whose daemon writes to a replaced log
(`logs_replaced`). A substring entry for the follower script cannot tell
the two followers apart, and a process quoting the command matches it.
The Claude login's ACCOUNT POOL. The login governs the token quota and nothing
else, so its accounts belong to no agent: any agent may be signed in with any
pool account, and SKILL.md step 5 says which one. Every path in this block is an
ABSOLUTE path, as its placeholder says; a leading ~ is expanded.
pool_file: PATH to the pool - a JSON LIST of { username, password, token_file,
home_agent }, mode 0600, outside this tree. NOT a credential - a path to one.
Shape: secrets/claude-account-pool.example.json. An account enters it ONLY
through `pool_pick.py --register <username> --token-stdin | --password-stdin`,
which also creates the pool, the lease file and the usage ledger when absent.
Read in-process by the pool picker (usernames only) and by signin_driver/ (the
chosen entry's password, typed into the field); nothing prints a credential.
lease_file: PATH to { "<username>": { "agent", "since" } } - which agent holds
which account. ONE account is live in ONE session at a time; the file has one
writer, the reviving agent, through `pool_pick.py --take`.
handover_ledger_file: PATH to the handover ledger, the markdown table
`pool_pick.py --take` appends one row to for every lease it moves or confirms
(and `--record` for every outcome). Optional: without it no row is written, and
the take's JSON says "handover_ledger": null. Under the reviving agent's home.
tokens_dir: where `--register --token-stdin` writes each account's token file,
<tokens_dir>/<username>.env, mode 0600 in a 0700 directory. Optional: the
default is claude-account-tokens beside the pool file. Organization secrets,
like the pool.
ledger_file: the usage ledger agent-health's parse_usage.py writes. The pick
predicts each account's weekly usage from it. The pick itself is agent-health's
pool_pick.py, the sibling skill in the fleet tree, which reads this block.
profiles_dir: the directory holding one STORED Chromium profile per pool
account, <profiles_dir>/<username>, made by enrolling it once with a person in
the loop (SKILL.md, 'Stored profiles'). A stored profile holds live Google and
claude.ai sessions for its account: it is a CREDENTIAL, so this belongs beside
the pool file in the organization secrets, never in a repository or an agent's
home - the driver REFUSES a profiles_dir inside a git work tree or under an
agents home, whatever this key says. The driver creates it mode 0700 at the
first enrollment and re-sets 0700 on every start; it need not exist before.
exclude: accounts no pick may name, each { username, reason } - e.g. one whose
sign-in is known broken. The reason is printed beside the account.
accounts.tokens_dir: <absolute path, beside the pool file, for the account tokens>
accounts.profiles_dir: <absolute path, beside the pool file, for the stored browser profiles>

exclude.username: <an account whose sign-in is known broken>

_comment: The Google 'Verify it's you' challenge route (SKILL.md step 6b, and step 7e's
human variant). Google can interpose that challenge during the sign-in and
send a verification code to the account's RECOVERY EMAIL; read_recovery_code.py
reads the code out of that mailbox by API and the reviver types it in.
mailbox: the recovery address every agent account carries (set per user in
the Workspace Admin console; one address for the whole fleet is what makes
this a config value rather than a per-agent lookup).
The token is minted by the google-spreadsheet skill's gsheets.py, the ONE
delegated-token minter on the machine, which read_recovery_code.py imports
from the sibling skill in the fleet tree rather than copying. The
service-account key that signs, and its delegation grant (which must list
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly), are that helper's own config
and CONTEXT.md; nothing here names a credential.
The tap-to-solve share (SKILL.md step 7; signin_driver/share.mjs owns the
mechanism). `signin.mjs <agent> share` shows the driver's own browser to ONE
person through x11vnc (vnc_port, 127.0.0.1 only), websockify serving noVNC
(web_port, 127.0.0.1 only) and a Tailscale Funnel on funnel_port, and tears all
of it down after `minutes` unless `unshare` comes first.
funnel_port: one the tailnet policy lets this node funnel (Tailscale allows 443,
8443 and 10000), and one NO other serve or funnel on the node uses - the share
refuses to start while the port serves anything, and its teardown turns that
port off. installation/check reads the node's funnel-ports capability.
novnc_dir: where the noVNC package installed its files (it must hold vnc.html).
page: the path and query the link opens on that port.
minutes: the default lifetime of a share; `share --minutes N` overrides it.
tailscale: the tailscale command as an argv array, with whatever lets it change
the funnel unattended (`sudo -n` where the agent's user is not the tailscale
operator). The public hostname is read from `tailscale status --json`
(Self.DNSName), so it is not configured anywhere.
